question: 92 mirrors were purchased for ₹92, and 35 mirrors broke in transit. The trader sold the remaining mirrors at ₹4.40 each. Find his profit.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of remaining mirrors to be sold = 92 − 35 = 57

Total Selling Price (SP) = 57 × 4.40 = ₹250.80

Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 250.80 − 92 = ₹158.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹158.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cost price of 92 mirrors (CP) = ₹92

Number of broken mirrors = 35

Selling price per remaining mirror = ₹4.40

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Total Selling Price (SP) − Total Cost Price (CP)

 
 CP = ₹92
 
 
 Profit = ₹158.80

 Total SP = ₹250.80

 Profit Calculation

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of mirrors remaining for sale = 92 − 35 = 57

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = 57 × 4.40

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = ₹250.80

⇒ Profit = Total SP − Total CP

⇒ Profit = 250.80 − 92

⇒ Profit = ₹158.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹158.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Loss and Loss Percentage

Loss occurs when Cost Price (CP) > Selling Price (SP). Loss = CP − SP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.
